messages:
Maria Chen: ran a quick nsys dump on ded10 (stable workload) after the rollout — top-kernel quantiles look odd, putting a lot of time into `softmax_forward` and `fused_attention_kv` compared to last week. attaching short summary:
```
nsys summary (top by total time):
softmax_forward           34.2%
fused_attention_kv        27.1%
kv_cache_lookup           12.3%
layernorm_fwd             6.0%
other                     20.4%
```
Observations: spike in softmax time at higher token lengths, and `kv_cache_lookup` shows a lot of small kernels firing (possible bank conflicts or non-optimal kernels). Anyone seen this pattern?

Josh Patel: :eyes: did this coincide with the batching heuristic change last deploy? iirc we bumped `batcher.max_batch_tokens`.

Li Wang: yep — `batcher.max_batch_tokens=8192` now (was 4096). that increases avg seq_len per launch. could push softmax into a different code path (tiling, wmma vs generic). also saw increased shared memory usage in perfetto for those launches.

Samir Gupta: can you paste the perfetto slice where softmax spikes? small kernels firing could be `kv_cache_lookup` microkernels from our KV path when cache misses cause per-token fallthrough.

Maria Chen: pasted a perfetto link: https://perfetto.local/trace/3344449999 (short slice around 00:12–00:16). also nvprof snippet below from the same run:
```
GPU Kernel: softmax_forward       Time  12.42ms  Avg 0.85ms  Calls 14
GPU Kernel: fused_attention_kv    Time  9.82ms   Avg 0.70ms  Calls 14
GPU Kernel: kv_cache_lookup       Time  4.46ms   Avg 0.31ms  Calls 14
```

Alex Romero: quick note — in nvprof the `softmax_forward` we use has two variants; the autotuner picks variant B for seq_len>=512 which has higher shared mem reuse but worse bank conflict behavior for certain heads. could be hitting that boundary more often.

nsys-bot: Trace uploaded: trace-3344449999-2026-03-18, size 48MB. Labels: nightly/throughput, env=dedicated-10.

Li Wang: i'll run a microbench that sweeps seq_len and batch_size to reproduce the quantile shift. plan: seq_len [128,256,384,512,768,1024], batch_tokens [2048,4096,8192,16384]. will run with and without `kv_cache` enabled. will post perfetto + nvprof snippets.

Josh Patel: also can we validate kernel selection thresholds? the tuner is currently picking based on `seq_len >= 512` and `heads >= 16`. maybe we should add an occupancy check before switching variants — if SM util < 60% we should prefer variant A.

Samir Gupta: agreed. i have a rough script to compute occupancy and warp efficiency from nsys outputs; i'll plug it into the trace-parsing job and tag launches where warp-stall > 30%.

Maria Chen: action items: (1) @Li Wang run microbench and post traces (due EOD), (2) @Josh Patel add a quick occupancy guard in the tuner config PR, (3) @Samir Gupta wire the warp/occupancy annotator into the nightly trace job. i'll collate and open a perf regression issue if we confirm.

Alex Romero: FYI i repro'd a small perf delta locally when forcing variant B at seq_len=384 with batch_tokens=8192 — ~8% slower p99 token latency. will add the repro command in the thread.

Li Wang: starting runs now, will tag traces as trace/maria-hotlist-3344449999.

Josh Patel: i'll draft the tuner guard PR and link to this thread.

Samir Gupta: prepping the parsing job, should have tagged runs by tomorrow AM.

Maria Chen: great. thanks all :thumbsup:
